primary.key: The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
primary.s: In a surah on the night of revelation, between the sending down and the angels’ descent, the ayah weighs the night’s worth; al-Tabari, on 97:1 to 97:5, reads it as deeds done that night outweighing the deeds of a thousand months that lack it.
primary.src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 97:1 to 97:5, the Tarteel QUL Arabic text via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

basis.words: وأشبه الأقوال في ذلك بظاهر التنزيل قول من قال: عملٌ في ليلة القدر خير من عمل ألف شهر، ليس فيها ليلة القدر.
basis.gloss: The view most in keeping with the plain wording of the revelation is that of those who said: deeds on the Night of Power are better than the deeds of a thousand months in which there is no Night of Power.

standby.key: Lo! it is thy insulter (and not thou) who is without posterity.
standby.s: After the Prophet is told of the abundance given him and bidden to pray and sacrifice, the surah turns to his detractor; al-Wahidi, on 108:1 to 108:3, reads it as revealed about al-As ibn Wa’il, who called him cut off after his son died.
standby.src: al-Wahidi, Asbāb al-nuzūl, on 108:1 to 108:3, ed. al-Humaydan (1992), OpenITI text at commit cc9beb0

basis.words: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في العاص بن وائل … قال: ذاك الأبتر، يعني النبي … وكان قد توفي قبل ذلك عبد الله ابن رسول الله … وكانوا يسمون من ليس له ابن: أبتر، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه السورة.
basis.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed about al-As ibn Wa’il … he said: that one who is cut off, meaning the Prophet … Abd Allah, the son of the Messenger of God, had died before that … and they used to call one who had no son cut off; so God sent down this surah.
